A bill for an act relating to higher education; requiring refund of unused student meal plan balances; requiring a report; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 135A.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[+[135A.196] REFUNDS FOR UNUSED MEAL PLAN BALANCES. +]

[+Subdivision 1.+]

[+Definitions.+]

[+(a) For the purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given. +]

[+(b) "Higher education institution" means any public or private postsecondary institution that is physically located in Minnesota that offers meal plans to students and receives federal or state financial aid funds on behalf of students. +]

[+(c) "Meal plan" means a prepaid plan offered by a higher education institution that provides students with access to campus dining services, including but not limited to meal swipes, dining dollars, or other credit-based systems for purchasing food and beverages on campus. +]

[+(d) "Unused balance" refers to any remaining funds or meal credits on a student's meal plan account that have not been used by the student as of 30 days after the end of the spring academic term, or the withdrawal or matriculation of the student, including: +]

[+(1) the cash value of any prepaid dollar or dollar-equivalent balance; and +]

[+(2) the cash value of any unused meal vouchers. +]

[+(e) "Federal or state financial aid" means financial assistance provided to students through programs authorized under federal or Minnesota state law, including grants, scholarships, loans, or other monetary assistance intended to support educational expenses. +]

[+(f) "Refund" means the return of unused balances to the student in the form of a check, electronic deposit, or credit applied to the student's account in compliance with this section. +]

[+Subd. 2.+]

[+Refund requirement.+]

[+(a) Not more than 45 days following the end of the spring academic term, or the withdrawal or matriculation of a student, a higher education institution must: +]

[+(1) refund any unused balance to a student; or +]

[+(2) at the student's request, apply the unused balance to the next academic term if the student has not withdrawn or matriculated. +]

[+(b) The Board of Regents of the University of Minnesota is requested to comply with this section. +]

[+Subd. 3.+]

[+Prohibition on meal plan fund forfeiture.+]

[+A higher education institution must not require students to forfeit unused balance or impose restrictions on the use of meal plan funds that result in financial disadvantage to a student. +]

[+Subd. 4.+]

[+Transparency and reporting.+]

[+(a) A higher education institution must provide a student with regular updates on the student's meal plan balance. +]

[+(b) A higher education institution must annually report meal plan balance refund practices and the higher education institution's compliance with this section to the commissioner of the Office of Higher Education. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to higher education; requiring refund of unused student meal plan balances; requiring a report; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 135A.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[135A.196] REFUNDS FOR UNUSED MEAL PLAN BALANCES.

Subdivision 1.

Definitions.

(a) For the purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.

(b) "Higher education institution" means any public or private postsecondary institution that is physically located in Minnesota that offers meal plans to students and receives federal or state financial aid funds on behalf of students.

(c) "Meal plan" means a prepaid plan offered by a higher education institution that provides students with access to campus dining services, including but not limited to meal swipes, dining dollars, or other credit-based systems for purchasing food and beverages on campus.

(d) "Unused balance" refers to any remaining funds or meal credits on a student's meal plan account that have not been used by the student as of 30 days after the end of the spring academic term, or the withdrawal or matriculation of the student, including:

(1) the cash value of any prepaid dollar or dollar-equivalent balance; and

(2) the cash value of any unused meal vouchers.

(e) "Federal or state financial aid" means financial assistance provided to students through programs authorized under federal or Minnesota state law, including grants, scholarships, loans, or other monetary assistance intended to support educational expenses.

(f) "Refund" means the return of unused balances to the student in the form of a check, electronic deposit, or credit applied to the student's account in compliance with this section.

Subd. 2.

Refund requirement.

(a) Not more than 45 days following the end of the spring academic term, or the withdrawal or matriculation of a student, a higher education institution must:

(1) refund any unused balance to a student; or

(2) at the student's request, apply the unused balance to the next academic term if the student has not withdrawn or matriculated.

(b) The Board of Regents of the University of Minnesota is requested to comply with this section.

Subd. 3.

Prohibition on meal plan fund forfeiture.

A higher education institution must not require students to forfeit unused balance or impose restrictions on the use of meal plan funds that result in financial disadvantage to a student.

Subd. 4.

Transparency and reporting.

(a) A higher education institution must provide a student with regular updates on the student's meal plan balance.

(b) A higher education institution must annually report meal plan balance refund practices and the higher education institution's compliance with this section to the commissioner of the Office of Higher Education.
